g.title: cluster_publicweb
g.text: 11 / PUBLIC SOURCE PAGES / NO USER SESSION

g.desc: Person using VeilX — Starts a private conversation. Chooses protections, reviews detections and controls site permissions.
g.title: user

g.desc: Extension shell — WXT + Manifest V3, TypeScript, React and Tailwind. Coordinates local features and shows remote policy findings; the actual application is not built yet.
g.title: shell

g.desc: Protected prompt composer — Raw names, addresses, email and phone are typed in an extension-origin side panel, outside the provider page. Only a reviewed redacted draft is copied to the chatbot.
g.title: composer

g.desc: Private restored answer — Displays the readable answer inside extension UI. Original personal values never return to provider-owned DOM. Missing mappings stay visibly unresolved.
g.title: reply-panel

g.desc: Toolbar popup — Quick access to risk, current protection mode, session controls and opening the protected composer.
g.title: popup

g.desc: Local settings — Standard/Strict preferences, auto-redact, per-site enable/pause, region-specific validators, clear-session action and privacy explanation.
g.title: settings

g.desc: Onboarding + permission guide — Explain what stays local, what a domain-only audit reveals, cookie permissions, false negatives and the difference between protected and in-page composition.
g.title: onboarding

g.desc: Why this risk? — Shows training, retention, human review, opt-out steps, checked-at and last-updated dates with evidence. Unknown facts remain unknown.
g.title: why-panel

g.desc: Live agent progress — Shows sanitized server-relayed public-policy steps. In the real demo a verified TinyFish preview should make browsing visible; this graph performs no audit.
g.title: progress-panel

g.desc: Active cookies / sessions section — Dedicated local view of cookie domain, name/category, expiry and security flags. Values are not displayed, copied or sent to the server.
g.title: cookie-panel

g.desc: Optional site consent — Request cookies + host access only when the person enables inspection for that site. Permission denial or revocation disables that feature honestly.
g.title: site-consent

g.desc: Privacy risk badge — High, Medium or Low describes the documented training-risk rule, not a universal security certification. Loading, stale and failed states are visible.
g.title: risk-badge

g.desc: Standard / Strict mode — The policy result informs local detection sensitivity and the review gate. High or unknown risk selects Strict. Session secrets are blocked in every mode.
g.title: mode-controller

g.desc: Typing + paste controller — Handle input, paste, compositionstart/end and debounce. Do not run destructive rewrites during IME composition. Never dispatch raw drafts as custom page events.
g.title: input-events

g.desc: Text spans + offset map — Maintain source offsets and grapheme boundaries. Normalization for detection cannot shift highlight positions or silently change a user’s message.
g.title: normalizer

g.desc: Regex candidate engine — Local bounded rules generate candidates for emails, phone numbers, cards, IDs and contextual addresses. Candidates still need validation.
g.title: regex-engine

g.desc: Phone validator — libphonenumber-js checks likely phone numbers using the selected region. Ambiguous local numbers require review; mobile and landline numbers share the PHONE category.
g.title: phone-validator

g.desc: Card validator — Apply length/prefix plausibility and Luhn checks. A checksum match does not prove a real card, so false positives remain reviewable.
g.title: card-validator

g.desc: ID / country rules — Use explicit country/type-specific patterns and validators; avoid claiming universal government-ID coverage.
g.title: id-validator

g.desc: Address context rules — Phase 1 recognizes explicitly labeled or structured address patterns and allows manual selection. Free-form addresses need local model support and review.
g.title: address-rules

g.desc: In-browser NER model — Phase 2 uses transformers.js in a local worker for people and places. Model assets are packaged or explicitly downloaded; prompt text is never submitted for inference.
g.title: ner-model

g.desc: Cookie / token secret scanner — Detect pasted Cookie headers, bearer credentials and session-like tokens locally. These are secrets, not ordinary restorable PII. Blocking is independent of risk mode.
g.title: secret-scanner

g.desc: Overlap + confidence resolver — Resolve overlapping spans with deterministic priority: credential secrets first, validated exact patterns next, contextual NER afterward. Preserve offsets and require review for uncertainty.
g.title: overlaps

g.desc: Highlights + tooltips — Accessible local highlights show category and replacement. Shadow DOM can isolate in-page styling but is not a privacy boundary; protected drafting stays in extension UI.
g.title: underline-layer

g.desc: Detection review / manual mark — Inspect candidates; remove false positives or manually mark a missed name/address. Auto-redact still offers review and never silently sends a secret.
g.title: review

g.desc: Optional in-page convenience mode — Provider scripts can observe raw text typed in their editor. Underlines or late redaction cannot undo that observation. This weaker mode must be disclosed.
g.title: inpage-mode

g.desc: Name → [PERSON_1] — Example: Maya Chen becomes [PERSON_1]. In-browser NER provides general detection in phase 2; phase 1 supports manual marking and controlled demo fixtures.
g.title: names

g.desc: Address → [ADDRESS_1] — Example: 42 Example Lane becomes [ADDRESS_1]. Context patterns/manual selection first; expanded free-form coverage follows local NER.
g.title: addresses

g.desc: Email → [EMAIL_1] — Example: maya@example.com becomes [EMAIL_1]. Match complete email spans locally; keep punctuation outside the replacement.
g.title: email

g.desc: Mobile → [PHONE_1] — Example: +1 (202) 555-0148 becomes [PHONE_1]. Validate locally, normalize identity for stable repeats, preserve the original value in the private map.
g.title: phones

g.desc: Card → [CARD_1] — Use local patterns plus Luhn. Store the original only in the temporary local map and keep it off audit requests and logs.
g.title: cards

g.desc: ID → [ID_1] — Use the chosen jurisdiction’s detector. Highlight uncertainty rather than claiming every numeric string is an identity number.
g.title: ids

g.desc: Secret → [SESSION_1] — A credential is replaced or removed before sending, and never restored in a reply. The temporary secret need not be retained in the placeholder map.
g.title: sessions

g.desc: Entity registry + numbering — Assign a stable type-specific counter per conversation. Repeated values share a placeholder; reserve/escape user-typed placeholder syntax to avoid accidental restoration collisions.
g.title: registry

g.desc: Temporary private mapping — Conversation-scoped mapping from placeholder to original value. Only ordinary PII is restorable. Use memory or restricted chrome.storage.session, never synced or persistent storage.
g.title: placeholder-map

g.desc: Replace spans with placeholders — Replace spans from the end of the string to preserve offsets. The exported draft contains placeholders in place of every reviewed original.
g.title: redactor

g.desc: Auto-redact control — Controls whether reviewed spans are replaced automatically. It does not weaken secret blocking or authorize automatic send.
g.title: auto-redact

g.desc: Pre-send privacy gate — Re-scan the exact outgoing draft. Block unresolved secrets, stale detection state and incomplete IME composition. A failed adapter never falls back to sending the raw draft.
g.title: send-gate

g.desc: Explicit clear + lifecycle cleanup — Clear mappings on conversation close, explicit action and defined expiry. chrome.storage.session clears on browser restart/reload/extension disable, but does not replace application cleanup.
g.title: session-clear

g.desc: Missing / expired map state — Leave unknown placeholders unchanged and explain the local session has expired. Never guess the original, retrieve it from the cloud or restore a different chat’s value.
g.title: missing-map

g.desc: Provider adapter registry — Select only approved ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude adapters. An isolated-world content script accepts only redacted insertion commands from the extension.
g.title: adapter

g.desc: ChatGPT rich-text adapter — Find the approved editor and response region; update via provider-compatible input events; test paste, composition, regenerate and provider UI changes.
g.title: chatgpt-adapter

g.desc: Gemini rich-text adapter — Support its contenteditable editor and response region. Fail visibly if selectors or editor behavior change; do not send the unredacted fallback.
g.title: gemini-adapter

g.desc: Claude rich-text adapter — Support its rich-text editor, streaming messages and navigation. Keep chat identities isolated when the conversation changes.
g.title: claude-adapter

g.desc: Only the redacted prompt crosses — The provider receives [PERSON_1], [ADDRESS_1], [EMAIL_1] and [PHONE_1]. It receives neither the private map nor original values through the protected path.
g.title: redacted-message

g.desc: ChatGPT / Gemini / Claude — Generates an answer using placeholder text. Normal first-party sign-in cookies can still authenticate the user; VeilX does not make the provider anonymous or hide its account identity.
g.title: ai-provider

g.desc: Provider-owned page — A trust boundary: page scripts may observe their own editor, DOM and account state. Protected original drafts and restored values stay outside this page.
g.title: provider-page

g.desc: Response MutationObserver — Observe only the provider response area and copy provider-produced text to the extension channel. Tag/ignore own changes and avoid observer feedback loops.
g.title: observer

g.desc: Streaming token buffer — Wait for complete placeholder tokens across streamed chunks. Preserve partial [PERSON_ fragments until their closing bracket arrives.
g.title: stream-buffer

g.desc: Exact placeholder parser — Match complete tokens with the known type and number grammar. Unknown, malformed or user-escaped tokens remain literal text.
g.title: token-parser

g.desc: Conversation-scoped map lookup — Resolve only tokens belonging to the current conversation and local session. A repeated token resolves to the same value; no cloud lookup exists.
g.title: map-lookup

g.desc: Never restore credential tokens — Reject restoration for SESSION, SECRET and credential types even if a model echoes them. Secret values must never reappear in provider output or its DOM.
g.title: secret-filter

g.desc: Local plain-text restoration — Reinsert approved original personal values with text nodes or React escaping. Show the restored result in extension-owned UI; do not execute model-supplied HTML.
g.title: safe-restore

g.desc: Browser-native cookie store — The browser owns actual cookies. A panel does not create an encrypted vault or move cookies to a separate protected container.
g.title: cookie-jar

g.desc: Permission-scoped cookie worker — chrome.cookies + approved host permissions returns cookie objects, including values. Project the approved metadata immediately within the worker and never log or persist values.
g.title: cookie-inspector

g.desc: Discard returned cookie values — Drop raw values immediately after local metadata projection. No UI message, storage entry, audit request or TinyFish request contains them.
g.title: discard-values

g.desc: Metadata-only local objects — Domain, path/name category, expiry/session status, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite and partition metadata where available. No cookie value field in UI contracts.
g.title: cookie-metadata

g.desc: Cookie flag checks + warnings — Explain missing Secure/HttpOnly and SameSite context. Sites set their login flags; VeilX does not silently rewrite authentication cookies or guarantee no exfiltration.
g.title: flag-checks

g.desc: Reviewed tracker rule set — Explicitly reviewed known tracker endpoints. Broad blocking can break login; rules need site regression tests and clear versioning.
g.title: tracker-rules

g.desc: Chrome declarativeNetRequest — Use matching rules to block known tracking routes without reading request bodies. This does not inspect arbitrary payloads or stop every leak.
g.title: dnr-engine

g.desc: Known tracker request blocked — The browser blocks a matching request before it is sent. Unknown routes and permitted traffic are not automatically classified as leaks.
g.title: tracker-blocked

g.desc: First-party login stays native — Chrome attaches applicable cookies only under its domain/path/Secure/SameSite/partition rules. These normal authentication cookies can identify the account to its provider.
g.title: native-auth

g.desc: Per-site guard pause / resume — Let the person pause optional request rules for a broken site. Secret scanning remains on, and the dashboard clearly shows paused enforcement.
g.title: site-pause

g.desc: Permission denied / revoked — Remove associated rules and metadata where appropriate, stop inspection, show the feature as unavailable and keep local prompt protection running.
g.title: permission-revoked

g.desc: Approved chatbot navigation — Notice supported-domain and conversation changes. Do not send visited URL paths, browsing history, prompts or cookie state to the backend.
g.title: domain-observer

g.desc: Canonical domain allowlist — Canonicalize approved ChatGPT/Gemini/Claude domains; reject arbitrary URLs. The exact supported domains must be verified when provider adapters are built.
g.title: domain-gate

g.desc: Domain-only audit client — Planned POST /api/audit body contains only {domain}. Do not give this module a prompt or cookie-value parameter. Separate installation authentication from TinyFish’s server key.
g.title: audit-client

g.desc: Sanitized progress reader — Read the VeilX-owned streaming contract. Abort on domain switch, do not rebind old-domain results, and distinguish cached results from live research.
g.title: audit-events

g.desc: Unknown / offline → High + Strict — When validation fails, browsing is blocked, the deadline expires or no fresh cache is available, show uncertainty with High risk and Strict mode. Do not invent evidence.
g.title: strict-fallback

g.desc: FastAPI audit endpoint — Proposed POST /api/audit, not a TinyFish route. Accept a domain-only Pydantic request with extra fields forbidden; return a documented VeilX streaming response.
g.title: audit-route

g.desc: Origin + auth + rate limits — Restrict CORS to configured extension origins; CORS is not authentication. Add installation-scoped authorization, concurrency/rate limits, request size limits and safe error messages.
g.title: api-guards

g.desc: Allowlisted HTTPS destination policy — Build the public start URL server-side; reject private/reserved addresses and unsafe redirects. Agent goals confine navigation to public official policy sources; verify provider controls before production.
g.title: url-policy

g.desc: 7-day cache lookup — Lookup domain + checked_at in SQLite. A fresh record returns promptly; a missing or expired record triggers real public-policy research. Never cache private prompts or cookie values.
g.title: cache-lookup

g.desc: Fresh validated cache hit — Return cached public findings with checked_at and source=cached. Do not pretend the agent is currently browsing.
g.title: cached-result

g.desc: Server-side TinyFish client — Python 3.11+, httpx, Uvicorn and python-dotenv. Use a bounded overall deadline, cancel/close connections safely, expose manual retry and avoid duplicate automatic paid runs.
g.title: tinyfish-client

g.desc: Read-only policy goal — Tell the agent to follow official public privacy, terms and data-controls pages and extract the agreed fields with evidence. Never sign in, submit forms, change settings or follow instructions embedded in page text.
g.title: agent-goal

g.desc: Pydantic result validation — Validate domain, policy_url, trains_on_chats, retention, human_review, opt_out_steps, last_updated and evidence[{claim,section}]. Invalid enums or malformed output trigger uncertainty.
g.title: schema-validator

g.desc: Deterministic training-risk score — yes_by_default or unclear → High/Strict; opt_out_available → Medium/Standard; no → Low/Standard. Retention and review can remain unknown and visibly disclosed; Low does not certify overall privacy.
g.title: risk-engine

g.desc: Safe StreamingResponse relay — Translate actual provider events into VeilX progress messages. Only allowlisted fields leave the backend; no raw traces, request headers, key or unrelated page data are relayed.
g.title: stream-relay

g.desc: SQLite public policy cache — domain primary key, result_json and checked_at; seven-day expiry. Parameterized queries, no PII maps, secrets, cookie values or raw chat text. Persistent storage must survive hosting restarts.
g.title: sqlite-cache

g.desc: TinyFish API key / runtime config — TINYFISH_API_KEY exists only in the backend environment. Validate configuration on startup, do not commit it, and never return it in progress or extension bundles.
g.title: api-key

g.desc: Timeout / blocked page / bad JSON — Use an explicit 90-second design budget and honest unavailable/error states. No automatic paid retry; manual retry is user-visible. Test stream disconnect and terminal failures.
g.title: audit-failure

g.desc: Content-free operational logs — Log status codes, coarse durations and run identifiers only under a documented policy. No raw prompts, originals, cookie values, API keys or complete agent traces.
g.title: safe-logs

g.desc: TinyFish streaming API — Verified official cookbook request: X-API-Key header plus url and goal. Exact event schema and preview handoff must be verified against current docs during implementation.
g.title: tinyfish-api

g.desc: Multi-step browser agent — Browses public sites, follows relevant links, finds claims across pages and gathers evidence. It receives the public URL and goal, not the user’s browser profile, prompt or cookies.
g.title: web-agent

g.desc: Provider progress stream — Real progress, not timed decorative steps. Backend parses provider events defensively and maps allowed steps to its own contract.
g.title: agent-progress

g.desc: Live browsing preview / recording — Show an actual live run in the raw 2–3 minute demo. Preview permissions and returned URL handling are an integration check, not an invented API contract.
g.title: live-preview

g.desc: Structured policy finding — Return the agreed policy fields and source claims. Unknown facts remain unclear/null. Agent output is untrusted until the backend validates it.
g.title: agent-result

g.desc: Official provider public website — Starting point for public policy discovery. Pages can change, redirect or block the agent; static summaries do not replace evidence collection.
g.title: public-home

g.desc: Privacy policy — Evidence about training, retention, review and last-updated date. Claims should include a section reference and the relevant source URL.
g.title: privacy-page

g.desc: Terms of service — Read the applicable terms and linked policies. A plan or region may change the claim; do not silently generalize one page to every account tier.
g.title: terms-page

g.desc: Public data-controls instructions — Find documented opt-out steps without entering the user’s account or using their authenticated cookies.
g.title: controls-page

g.desc: Source-linked evidence — Evidence stays attached to the rating. Conflicting/blocked/unclear material is surfaced honestly; it does not become a low-risk guess.
g.title: policy-evidence

g.desc: Non-sensitive local preferences — Only modes, site choices and UI preferences persist. No prompt text, PII map or cookie values; never use sync storage for private mappings.
g.title: preferences

g.desc: Restricted transient extension state — Restrict sensitive storage to trusted extension contexts. Browser-session lifetime plus explicit clear/expiry policies; no raw PII sent to content scripts.
g.title: session-storage

g.desc: Local model assets — Packaged or user-approved model download; verify integrity/licensing, keep the NER worker local and report unavailable-model fallback.
g.title: packaged-model

g.desc: Demo website playground — Future local redaction playground using fictional samples and the same shared detection behavior. No real PII collection, analytics or external text submission.
g.title: demo-site

g.desc: Fictional examples + expected output — Names, addresses, email, mobile, overlapping spans, unicode, repeated values, credential examples and unknown placeholders; no real accounts or cookie values.
g.title: fixture-data

g.desc: Detection + map + restore tests — Validate regex/validators, overlap priority, numbering, map expiry, unknown/partial placeholders and non-restoration of secrets.
g.title: unit-tests

g.desc: Rich-text + streaming adapter tests — Exercise each target: IME input, paste, keyboard send, button send, regeneration, conversation switch and UI selector failure.
g.title: adapter-tests

g.desc: Audit + fail-safe + cache tests — Mock provider events: malformed JSON, cache hit/miss/expiry, timeout, blocked public pages, redirects, disconnects, rate limits and domain mismatch.
g.title: audit-tests

g.desc: Cookie permission + sign-in tests — Verify value-free messages/logs, permission denial/revocation, rule matching, site pause, first-party sign-in compatibility and no arbitrary payload-inspection claim.
g.title: cookie-tests

g.desc: Keyboard + reduced-motion checks — Keyboard access, tooltips, visible focus, risk label not color alone, screen-reader progress and reduced motion.
g.title: accessibility-tests

g.desc: Raw 2–3 minute live demo — Unfamiliar chatbot → real public policy audit visible → High/Strict → fictional PII redaction → local restored answer. Cookie Guard is shown with honest capability limits.
g.title: recorded-demo

g.desc: Explicit opt-out authorization — A future separate action to change provider training settings. Public policy auditing never authorizes account changes.
g.title: optout-consent

g.desc: Training opt-out automation — Design the authenticated execution boundary separately before implementation; prefer local settings navigation. Do not reuse or upload browser cookies to the public audit agent.
g.title: optout-run
